title: Strict quotient balancing and pullback preserve the quotient augmentation
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I$ a finitely generated ideal, $A/I$ additive torsion, and $P_n=A/I^n$ finite and perfect over $A$ for every $n\geq1$. For a scheme $T$, use its small pro-etale site, the constant ring sheaves $\underline A_T$, $\underline{P_n}_T$, and $A_T=\varprojlim_n\underline{P_n}_T$, with canonical scalar map $\underline A_T\to A_T$ and quotient projections [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. All sites are small in [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $D(A_T)$ and $D(\underline A_T)$ for unbounded derived module categories and $r_T$ for restriction along this scalar map [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op}$, $\Delta$ be its constant-diagram functor, and $Q_T=(\underline{P_n}_T)_n$ with quotient transitions. On the ringed diagram site [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], define $\mathcal R_T^aL=\Delta L\otimes^L_{\Delta A_T}Q_T$ and $\mathcal R_T^0L_0=\Delta L_0\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_T}Q_T$. These are actual derived strict towers. For an edge $u:U\to V$ use the canonical coefficient isomorphisms $u^{-1}A_V\cong A_U$, $u^{-1}\underline{P_n}_V\cong\underline{P_n}_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image], the ordinary ringed operations $L_u^a\dashv R_u^a$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], their strict-diagram operations $\mathscr L_u^a\dashv\mathscr R_u^a$, and the constant-coefficient counterparts $G_u\dashv R_u^0$ and $G_u\dashv R_u^{\mathcal T}$. Let $a_u:r_UL_u^a\cong G_ur_V$, $\chi_u:r_VR_u^a\cong R_u^0r_U$, $p_u:r_U\mathscr L_u^a\cong G_ur_V$ and $d_u:r_V\mathscr R_u^a\cong R_u^{\mathcal T}r_U$ be the normalized flat scalar comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction].

For every ambient $L\in D(A_T)$ there is a natural strict-diagram balancing isomorphism $\rho_L:r_T\mathcal R_T^aL\cong\mathcal R_T^0r_TL$. On a flat-term K-flat representative it is the balancing map identifying the two quotient diagrams, sending each tensor class to itself, with all quotient transitions. It satisfies the strict augmentation equation $\rho_Lr_T(\Delta L\to\mathcal R_T^aL)=(\Delta r_TL\to\mathcal R_T^0r_TL)$ under $r_T\Delta\cong\Delta r_T$. Here K-flat means tensoring with the complex takes acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Let $\tau_{u,L}:\mathcal R_U^aL_u^aL\cong\mathscr L_u^a\mathcal R_V^aL$ be canonical pullback/tensor reassociation [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Set $q_{u,L}=(G_u\rho_L)p_{u,\mathcal R_V^aL}$. Then
$$q_{u,L}\,r_U(\tau_{u,L})=\mathcal R_U^0(a_{u,L})\rho_{L_u^aL},$$
where the right side uses the canonical identification $\mathcal R_U^0G_u\cong G_u\mathcal R_V^0$.

All these are natural isomorphisms and equalities in the actual derived strict-tower category, on arbitrary ambient inputs.

proof.text: Put $R_T=\underline A_T$, $B_T=A_T$, $S_{T,n}=\underline{P_n}_T$, and $J_{T,n}=I^nR_T$. The constant-module functor preserves cokernels and finite sums [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-constant-exact]. Apply it to a finite-generator presentation $A^e\to A\to A/I^n\to0$; the image is precisely $I^nR_T$, so $R_T/J_{T,n}=S_{T,n}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], $B_T$ is flat over $R_T$ and its specified projection induces $B_T/J_{T,n}B_T\cong S_{T,n}$. These are the common-quotient hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-common-quotient-reduction-tower]. Their compatibility for $b\geq a$ follows by composing the projections: both quotient maps take the class of $z$ to its class modulo $I^a$. The finiteness hypothesis identifies these constant quotient sheaves with the coefficient sheaves of the item. No completeness condition on the input complex is used.

source.place: Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat), applied to ideal powers; constant-sheaf cokernels

proof.text: Choose one flat-term K-flat $B_T$-complex $P$ representing $L$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Flat restriction makes $r_TP$ K-flat with flat $R_T$-terms [lem-weil-pbc-flat-scalar-restriction-kflat]. On the small diagram site [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], $\Delta P$ is K-flat: if a diagram complex $E$ is acyclic, $(E\otimes\Delta P)(n)=E(n)\otimes P$ is acyclic for every $n$, by [def-pc-kflat-complex]; here evaluation at $n$ is the module inverse image along $e_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], so it carries the diagram-site tensor to the tensor of the evaluations [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison], and cohomology is computed levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. The same argument applies to $\Delta r_TP$. Tensor and its total complex have the componentwise formulas of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on that small site to the ring maps $\Delta B_T\to Q_T$ and $\Delta R_T\to Q_T$, then restrict the resulting $Q_T$-modules along the same maps. Thus the two reductions in the item are computed by the actual complexes of strict towers $(P\otimes_{B_T}S_{T,n})_n$ and $(r_TP\otimes_{R_T}S_{T,n})_n$.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); the same constructions on the small diagram site

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-common-quotient-reduction-tower] using step 1 and $P$. Take the inverse of its comparison, so the direction is $\rho_P:(r_T(P\otimes_{B_T}S_{T,n}))_n\to(r_TP\otimes_{R_T}S_{T,n})_n$. It and its inverse send $p\otimes s$ to $p\otimes s$, interpreted as pure sections of sheaf tensors [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. The cited theorem supplies naturality in $P$, the chain-map property, all quotient transitions, and the strict quotient cone. In particular $\rho_P(p\otimes1)=p\otimes1$ in every degree and level. Restriction of scalars leaves the underlying sheaves and maps unchanged [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], so $r_T\Delta P=\Delta r_TP$ with their identical transition maps. Consequently $\rho_P r_T(\Delta P\to\mathcal R_T^aP)=(\Delta r_TP\to\mathcal R_T^0r_TP)$ is already an equality of chain maps of strict towers.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product); common-quotient balancing, transitions and quotient cones as stated in lem-weil-pbc-flat-common-quotient-reduction-tower

proof.text: For $u:U\to V$, the specified coefficient isomorphisms identify $u^{-1}B_V=B_U$ and $u^{-1}S_{V,n}=S_{U,n}$ and commute with both projections and all quotient maps [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. The constant-ring identification $u^{-1}R_V\cong R_U$ carries each constant scalar to the same scalar [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. It also commutes with $R_T\to B_T$: after every finite projection it sends each constant $a$ to its same residue class; the limit projections determine the ring map. Thus the flat scalar comparison hypotheses hold by step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction], ordinary and diagram pullbacks are exact inverse image on the underlying module sheaves, and $a_u,p_u$ are the normalized identifications of these inverse images. Set $P_u=u^*P$, with the transported $B_U$-action. It represents $L_u^aL$ and is K-flat with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Its restriction represents $G_ur_VL$ by step 2 and $a_u$. This uses coefficient-ring isomorphisms, not a flatness assertion for the morphism of schemes.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); exact inverse image for the coefficient-ring identifications

proof.text: The ordinary inverse-image tensor comparison sends the inverse image of a pure tensor to the pure tensor of the inverse images [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison]. With the ring identifications of step 4 it gives, in each degree, $u^*(P\otimes_{B_V}S_{V,n})\cong P_u\otimes_{B_U}S_{U,n}$, and the identical formula over $R$. These are maps of strict diagrams: their naturality in the second factor includes every $S_{V,b}\to S_{V,a}$. They compute the canonical derived comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], although $Q_V$ need not be flat. Indeed resolve $Q_V$ on the small diagram site by a flat-term K-flat complex [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Tensoring this resolution with $\Delta P$ is a quasi-isomorphism by its K-flatness, and exact inverse image preserves it. On the two K-flat factors the derived comparison is the ordinary total tensor comparison; its naturality gives the same comparison after inverting this quasi-isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Thus $\tau_{u,L}$ is represented by the inverse of this ordinary tensor comparison; the canonical $\mathcal R_U^0G_u\cong G_u\mathcal R_V^0$ is represented by its constant-ring counterpart.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), proof by K-flat representatives; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback)

proof.text: Compare the two asserted composites on the representative with level $P_u\otimes_{B_U}S_{U,n}$. Under step 5 write the inverse image of a tensor as $x\otimes s$, using the generalized pure pairing. On the left, $\tau$ gives that inverse-image tensor, $p_u$ keeps its underlying tensor, and $G_u\rho_P$ changes its balancing ring from $B$ to $R$, giving $x\otimes s$. On the right, $\rho_{P_u}$ first changes the balancing ring to $R_U$, $\mathcal R_U^0(a_u)$ keeps $x\otimes s$, and the constant-ring comparison gives the same inverse-image tensor. Pure sections determine linear maps out of the sheaf tensor [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus], so these maps are equal in every degree as sheaf maps. For the differential both formulas give $d(x)\otimes s$, and for a transition $b\to a$ both give $x\otimes q_{b,a}(s)$; the coefficient comparison commutes with $q_{b,a}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Therefore this is an equality of maps of strict diagram complexes, not merely an equality of maps after evaluation in separate derived categories. This proves the required formula on the representative, with the stated direction of $q_{u,L}$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), determination by pure tensors; explicit representative calculation

proof.text: The flat-term K-flat homotopy category localized at its quasi-isomorphisms is equivalent to $D(B_T)$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Both strict reduction functors invert quasi-isomorphisms on this class: use the two diagram-site scalar extensions of step 2 and [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], with flat restriction for the second. Pullback in step 4 is exact, hence also inverts these maps. The comparisons of steps 3 and 5 and their inverses are natural in chain maps; their degreewise tensor formulas respect chain homotopies. They therefore descend along that localization equivalence to natural isomorphisms in the actual derived strict-tower category. The strict augmentation equality of step 3 and the strict equality of step 6 descend as equalities under the same functor. This defines $\rho_L$ independently of the chosen representative and proves the augmentation and pullback equations on every ambient input. The localization takes place with the strict-tower category as target throughout; no faithfulness assertion for level evaluations in a derived category is used.

tool_uses.why: General flat-term K-flat resolution existence on arbitrary small ringed sites, including the strict diagram site; no replacement of the unit proper-base-change route.
General K-flat computation and quasi-isomorphism invariance for scalar extension, applied to the two maps of ring sheaves on the small diagram site.

Canonical identification of the inverse image of the constant ring sheaf of A (not finite, so lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image does not give it) with the constant ring sheaf, carrying constants to constants; needed for the constant-coefficient side G_u and for the hypothesis a_U c_R = c_S u^{-1} a_V of lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction. Already used in this unit by lem-weil-pbc-pulled-reduction-strict-tower-comparison.

NZ created it as a statement-only node; its base proof was empty, it has no repair note and it is not on the 10-19 dropped list. The delivery is 7 steps with 0 new nodes, and the statement is unchanged. I read every cited statement and did not find a false step. Step 1: the common-quotient hypotheses come from constant-exact (the cokernel of A^e→A gives image I^n·R) and from constant-completion-equivalence (flatness and A_T/I^n ≅ P_n, matching Stacks 093M at sites-modules.tex:8261). Step 3: the direction of ρ is the inverse of the common-quotient comparison. p⊗s ↦ p⊗s holds because both sides are identified with P/J_nP and s is locally r·1. The augmentation equation holds at chain level. Step 4: the datum requires P_n to be finite as a set, so the profinite node applies. Pullback along the coefficient isomorphisms is exact. Step 5: Q_V is not flat; the step handles this with a K-flat resolution and exact u^*. Step 6: I re-did the pure-tensor chase; both sides give u^{-1}(p⊗_R s), and differentials and transitions agree. Step 7: the maps descend through the site-derived-tensor-descent equivalence. Edge cases I=0, I=A, identity u and n=1 are fine. The closure has no cycle, no trf node, no SGA source and no dropped node. Overlap with pulled-reduction-strict-tower-comparison and constant-completion-equivalence is advisory only. (2) Step 2 used levelwise tensor on the diagram site without a citation; I named evaluation as the inverse image along e_n and cited lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison. proof_deps is recomputed.
